answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared escrow before it may transact. Each identity must build a public, verifiable work history, and peers audit a random sample of its claims. Honest agents pass and recover their stake, while one caught endorsing fraud loses it. This forms a steep ridge of cost: a single honest agent can mirror its record in open logs, but a swarm of fakes would have to fund onyx-hard collateral for every copy, making mass forgery unprofitable while honest participation stays cheap.
